content: Humana Inc., established in 1961 in Louisville, Kentucky, is a Fortune 500 company specializing in marketing and administering health benefit consumer services. The company generates $4 billion in revenue and employs over 25,000 associates across the United States, Puerto Rico, and Western Europe. In March 2007, Fortune Magazine recognized Humana as one of the Top 5 Most Admired Healthcare Companies in the United States. The company was originally founded by David Jones and Wendell Cherry as a nursing home business under the name Extendicare. By the 1970s, Extendicare had become the largest nursing home company in the United States. In 1972, the company shifted its focus to acquiring hospitals, eventually becoming the largest hospital company in the world by the 1980s. To reflect this new direction, the company was renamed Humana Inc. in 1974. Humana experienced significant growth during this period, including the acquisition of American Medicorp Inc. in 1978, which doubled its size. The company also implemented a fast-track construction process, completing one hospital per month, and developed the innovative double-corridor hospital design to improve efficiency and patient care. In the 1980s, Humana created an integrated healthcare delivery system with flexible health plans and began marketing health insurance in 1984. The company also established the Humana Heart Institute in 1985, bringing groundbreaking artificial heart research to Louisville. By the 1990s, Humana transitioned into a consumer health benefits company, spinning off its hospital operations into a new entity, Galen Health Care Inc., in 1993. Galen later merged with Columbia/HCA. In 1998, United Healthcare attempted to acquire Humana but failed due to financial losses. In 1999, Humana pioneered consumer-driven healthcare services, launching its first offerings on September 11, 2001. The company introduced health savings account services in 2003 and partnered with Richard Branson's Virgin Group in 2005. In 2005, Humana was chosen as the administrative partner for the Business Health Care Group of Southeast Wisconsin, implementing strategies to reduce healthcare costs and improve transparency. Following the passage of the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act, Humana launched a nationwide campaign in 2006 to promote Medicare Advantage and Prescription Drug Plans, signing up approximately 5 million consumers and becoming the second-largest provider in the senior market. That same year, Humana introduced RightSource, a national mail-order pharmacy business. Humana's headquarters in Louisville, Kentucky, is a notable example of postmodern architecture, designed by Michael Graves and completed in 1985. The company also occupies several other buildings in downtown Louisville and has undertaken historic preservation projects in the area. Humana employs over 8,500 people in downtown Louisville and works with preservation experts to maintain the historic integrity of its properties. Michael B. McCallister, a 33-year company veteran, serves as Humana's President and CEO. He began his career in 1974 as a financial analyst and was recognized by Forbes Magazine in 2006 as one of the most successful CEOs in creating shareholder value. David Jones Jr., son of the company's founder, is the Chairman of the Board of Directors. The Humana Foundation donates millions annually to nonprofit organizations in its business markets. It sponsors the Humana Festival of New American Plays, an internationally renowned event held at Louisville's Actors Theatre. The foundation also contributed $1 million to the Gulf Coast region following Hurricane Katrina. Humana has faced controversies, including a 1987 lawsuit against NBC over a storyline in the medical drama St. Elsewhere and criticism from Linda Peeno, a former contractor, who testified before Congress about the downsides of managed care. Peeno's testimony was featured in Michael Moore's 2007 documentary Sicko, which also highlighted other disputes involving Humana. The company has disputed some of these claims, emphasizing the validity of its coverage decisions based on specific healthcare plans. Humana is also involved in military healthcare as a TRICARE Regional Contractor for the Southern United States. The company has a long-standing relationship with the PGA Tour and Champions Tour, serving as their Official Health Benefits Provider. Additionally, Humana associates act as an internal test market for the company's next-generation consumer services.
